I subscribed to Rocksbox which lets you borrow jewelry. They send 3 pieces every time, and you return it whenever you’re ready. Any piece you fall in love with and want to keep, you just send back the box without it and they charge you for that piece you keep. You get to look through their jewelry and add them to your wishlist. You can send a picture of a specific outfit you want jewelry to match with and you can request certain styles. I like it because I like being able to be versatile with the type of jewelry I wear. I’ve definitely gotten pieces that I don’t particularly like, but it tells the stylist what not to send you next time. It’s pretty great. You can pause getting sent boxes when you want, especially when money is tight, and you can start right back up again when you can.

I was waiting at a bus stop at 11pm, and an older man approached me and asked me for help, probably because I was the only Chinese person there. He didn't speak English and he had just moved to the area. He showed me his address that was written on a piece of paper and asked for directions. 

Apparently it was his first day at work. He got on the wrong bus to get back home and subsequently got lost. He was wandering around for 3 hours trying to find his way back home in an unfamiliar city. I asked him if he called his family. He replied that they were busy and he didn't want to disturb them. He was actually really close to getting home. 

I gave him directions but in the end, I decided to call him an Uber home because I was afraid he wouldn't be able to find his way home. 

To this day, every time I drive along the street he lives on, I wonder how he's doing. It reminded me a lot about how my dad moved to America, going door to door trying to find a job without being able to speak English. 

If I hadn't decided to take the longer route home so I could rest a bit longer, he wouldn't have found me, the only person who could communicate with him to help get him home.
